label: Absurdist
definition: Drama and film in which conventional plot, characterization and logic are ignored or distorted to convey the irrationality of existence and humanity's isolation in a meaningless world, as in the post-war Theatre of the Absurd.
performerDemands: Precise control of pauses, rhythm and silence, and full commitment to illogical lines while holding comedy and despair together.

label: Action
definition: A film genre that predominantly features chase sequences, fights, shootouts, explosions and stunt work.
performerDemands: Physical fitness, fight choreography and stunt work, with a believable physical presence under pressure.
demandsSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film (names stunt work as a defining feature; actor preparation not discussed)

label: Action Comedy
definition: A genre combining action and comedy, with fast action that stays mostly lighthearted and rarely involves death or serious injury.
performerDemands: Comic timing and character-driven humour delivered alongside physical action, chase and fight work.
demandsSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_comedy (the genre 'relies on the characters to bring out the humor')

label: Adventure
definition: A film genre whose plots feature travel, typically sending protagonists away from home to distant or exotic places to fulfil a goal such as a quest or search.
performerDemands: Heroic physical presence and stamina for location work and set pieces, with an appealing, resourceful screen persona.

label: Alternate History
definition: A genre of fiction that imagines a different course of history following a changed key event or figure, and explores the consequences of that point of divergence.
performerDemands: Grounded, period-appropriate playing that makes an altered world feel lived-in and plausible.

label: Animated
definition: Films made from a series of drawings, computer graphics or photographed objects such as puppets or models that, viewed in quick succession, create the appearance of movement.
performerDemands: Voice acting: carrying character, emotion and comedy through the voice alone, often recorded apart from scene partners.

label: Anime
definition: A style of animation originating in Japan, used in Japanese films and television programmes, known for colourful images, strong characters and action-heavy stories.
performerDemands: Voice acting in a heightened, expressive register, often including dubbing to match existing lip movements and timing.

label: Anthology
definition: A single film or series made of several self-contained shorter stories, often by different directors or writers, tied together by a shared theme, premise or framing device.
performerDemands: Establishing a character quickly in a short segment, and often playing different roles across segments.

label: Apocalyptic
definition: A subgenre of science fiction concerned with the end of civilization through nuclear war, plague, natural disaster or another existential catastrophe.
performerDemands: Sustained fear, grief and desperation played truthfully at extreme stakes.

label: Art House
definition: Films made primarily as serious artistic expression rather than for commercial success, often experimental and aimed at a niche rather than a mass audience.
performerDemands: Restrained, interior and often ambiguous performance, sustained in long takes with little explanatory dialogue.

label: Avant-Garde
definition: Filmmaking that rejects standard cinematic conventions in favour of non-narrative forms or alternatives to traditional narratives and methods of working.
performerDemands: Openness to non-naturalistic, stylized or movement-based work, sometimes without character or dialogue.

label: Backstage Musical
definition: A musical whose plot is set in a theatrical context and revolves around putting on a play or revue, with songs performed as diegetic numbers within that show.
performerDemands: Singing and dancing at a performance-within-the-story standard, alternating with dramatic scenes.

label: Biker
definition: A film genre, regarded as a branch of exploitation film, portraying motorcycle-riding rebels who usually belong to an outlaw motorcycle club.
performerDemands: Motorcycle riding skills and a rough, rebellious physical presence.

label: Biographical
definition: A film that dramatizes the life, or the defining period of the life, of a real person or group of people under their real names.
performerDemands: Research-based portrayal of a real person, often including matching voice, mannerisms and physical appearance across years.

label: Black Comedy
definition: Comedy that juxtaposes morbid or ghastly elements with comic ones to underscore the senselessness or futility of life.
performerDemands: Playing grim situations with deadpan sincerity and precise comic timing, without signalling the joke.

label: Blaxploitation
definition: A 1970s subgenre of American exploitation film featuring Black protagonists, made for African American urban audiences and often dealing with crime, drugs, violence and racial conflict.
performerDemands: Charismatic, larger-than-life star presence with streetwise swagger and action work.

label: Body Horror
definition: A subgenre of horror that showcases grotesque or disturbing violations of the human body, such as mutation, disease, mutilation or uncontrolled transformation.
performerDemands: Long hours in prosthetics, physically committed transformation, and conveying pain and loss of bodily control.

label: Buddy Comedy
definition: A subgenre in which two people, usually with contrasting personalities, go on an adventure, mission or trip and build a friendship through comic friction.
performerDemands: Double-act chemistry, quick back-and-forth banter and comic timing with a scene partner.

label: Buddy Cop
definition: A film and television genre in which two people of very different personalities, usually police officers or agents, are forced to work together to solve a crime.
performerDemands: Partner chemistry and contrasting temperaments, combining banter with action and stunt work.

label: Caper
definition: A lighter-toned subgenre of crime fiction in which a team of skilled rogues plans and executes a daring, elaborate crime, emphasizing wit and cleverness over violence.
source: https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Caper_story (Wikipedia mirror, 'Caper story'); https://www.bfi.org.uk/lists/10-great-caper-films (BFI, found but not read)
performerDemands: Charm, light comic timing and ensemble play, with each character's specialty established quickly.

label: Chanbara
definition: The Japanese 'sword-fighting' film genre, a sub-category of jidaigeki (period drama) centred on samurai and their swordplay.
performerDemands: Choreographed swordplay and martial bearing, with period movement and stillness.

label: Chase
definition: Films in which a chase or race is the primary plot element, a form dating to early cinema and its comic chase films.
source: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q16538713 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Chase_films (Wikipedia/Wikidata); Oxford Reference entry 'Chase film' found but returned 403
performerDemands: Physical stamina, running and stunt work, and sustained urgency across action sequences.

label: Children’s
definition: Films made specifically for children, typically with child protagonists, age-appropriate content and a clear moral message.
performerDemands: Warm, clear and energetic playing readable by young audiences; often work by child actors.

label: Christmas
definition: Films set around Christmas in which the season meaningfully shapes the story, commonly with themes of family, goodwill and reunion, and combinable with almost any other genre.
performerDemands: Sincere warmth and sentiment without irony, often in family-comedy register.

label: Comedy
definition: A genre that treats the light and amusing, or the serious in a light, familiar or satirical manner, with the aim of amusing its audience.
source: https://www.britannica.com/art/comedy (Encyclopaedia Britannica; fetch returned 403, read via search)
performerDemands: Comic timing: control of pauses, cadence, delivery and pacing to land a joke, and listening to scene partners.

label: Coming Of Age
definition: Stories that follow a young protagonist through the transition from childhood to adulthood, focused on growth and the loss of innocence.
performerDemands: Truthful, unforced emotional performance of youth and personal change, driven by dialogue rather than action.

label: Concert Film
definition: A film whose content consists primarily of footage of an extended live music performance before an audience.
performerDemands: Live musical performance and stage presence sustained for camera.

label: Conspiracy Thriller
definition: A thriller in which the protagonist confronts a large, powerful hidden conspiracy whose extent only they recognize.
performerDemands: Sustained tension and growing paranoia, played with restraint.

label: Cosmic Horror
definition: A subgenre of horror, also called Lovecraftian horror, built on dread of the unknowable and humanity's insignificance before vast, indifferent forces, favouring psychological horror over gore.
performerDemands: Escalating dread and the portrayal of a mind unravelling, often reacting to what cannot be shown.

label: Costume Drama
definition: A film or television drama set in the past in which the actors wear the costumes of a former age.
performerDemands: Period manners, deportment and speech, and moving naturally in period clothing such as corsets.

label: Courtroom Drama
definition: A genre of film and television, also called legal drama, in which a system of justice and its legal proceedings play a critical role in the narrative.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_drama (Wikipedia; also cites the AFI definition)
performerDemands: Sustained, precise delivery of long argumentative speeches and testimony, with emotional restraint under cross-examination.

label: Creature Feature
definition: A subgenre of horror and science fiction in which a monster or creature serves as the primary antagonist to humans.
source: https://nofilmschool.com/creature-feature (No Film School; Wikipedia 'Monster movie' listed alongside)
performerDemands: Convincing fear and reaction work against creatures that are often absent, puppeteered or added later in post-production.

label: Crime
definition: A film genre in which crime, its motives, methods, investigation and consequences, is the key element of the plot.
performerDemands: Grounded, morally ambiguous characterisation and controlled menace or tension.

label: Cyberpunk
definition: A subgenre of science fiction set in a bleak, high-tech near future where advanced computing and cybernetics coexist with social decay and corporate oppression.
source: https://guides.lib.utexas.edu/c.php?g=849284&p=9855392 (University of Texas at Austin library glossary of science-fiction genres)
performerDemands: Hard-boiled, noir-inflected performance within heavily stylised, effects-driven environments, often with action and fight work.

label: Dance
definition: A film, also called screen dance, in which dancing is used to reveal the film's challenges and central themes, whether narrative or formal.
performerDemands: Trained dance technique and stamina, with choreography performed repeatedly for the camera.

label: Dark Fantasy
definition: A subgenre of fantasy that combines magical and supernatural elements with the grim, unsettling and macabre atmosphere of horror.
performerDemands: Heightened, morally ambiguous characterisation sustained amid prosthetics, costume and effects-heavy settings.

label: Detective
definition: A story dealing with the step-by-step investigation and solution of a crime, usually murder, by a professional or amateur detective.
performerDemands: Clear, observant intelligence conveyed through deduction scenes and lengthy expository revelations.

label: Disaster
definition: A film genre that has an impending or ongoing disaster, natural or man-made, as its subject and primary plot device.
performerDemands: Large-ensemble work sustaining panic, peril and physical endurance, often on effects stages or in water and stunt sequences.

label: Docudrama
definition: A drama, as for television, dealing freely with historical events, especially of a recent and controversial nature.
performerDemands: Accurate portrayal of real, often living people, including their voice, manner and appearance.

label: Docufiction
definition: The cinematographic combination of documentary and fiction, in which real people and settings are placed within a fictionalised narrative.
performerDemands: Naturalistic, unadorned behaviour; participants often play themselves or near-versions of themselves, frequently as non-professional actors.

label: Documentary
definition: A motion picture that shapes and interprets factual material for purposes of education or entertainment.
performerDemands: Little conventional acting; narration and voice-over work, or reconstruction scenes, are the usual roles for actors.

label: Domestic Drama
definition: Drama centred on the private and family affairs of ordinary, usually middle-class, people rather than on public matters of state (descended from the older form called domestic tragedy).
source: https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/oi/authority.20110803095725766 (Oxford Reference, 'domestic tragedy'; Wikipedia 'Domestic drama' also listed)
performerDemands: Intimate, naturalistic ensemble acting conveying family tension and everyday emotional detail.

label: Drama
definition: A play, film or television programme about a serious subject that is not primarily meant to make the audience laugh.
performerDemands: Emotional truthfulness and psychological depth sustained across a character's arc.

label: Dystopian
definition: Fiction set in a dystopia, an imagined society in which people are unhappy and usually afraid because they are not treated fairly; the opposite of a utopia.
performerDemands: Conveying suppressed fear and resistance under an oppressive system, often with restrained, controlled performance.

label: Eco-Horror
definition: A subgenre of horror, also called eco-terror, concerned with human fear for and of the non-human natural world, often as a consequence of human damage to it.
source: https://writingwerewolf.substack.com/p/what-is-eco-horror (blog; Wikipedia 'List of eco-horror films' and MUBI Notebook primer also listed, no encyclopaedic entry found)
performerDemands: Sustained dread and survival-driven physical performance, often reacting to unseen or effects-generated threats.

label: Epic
definition: A film genre of grand scale and sweeping scope, typically dealing with historical events or legendary heroic figures, with large casts and lavish settings.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film (Wikipedia; filmsite.org AFI genre page also listed)
performerDemands: Commanding, heightened presence and oratory, with period manners, costume, horse and battle work across a long shoot.

label: Erotic Thriller
definition: A film subgenre of the thriller with a thematic basis in illicit romance or sexual fantasy, holding pleasure and danger in close proximity.
performerDemands: Seductive, guarded performances balancing sexual intimacy scenes with sustained suspense and deception.

label: Espionage
definition: A genre, also called the spy film or spy thriller, that deals with fictional espionage, either realistically or as a basis for fantasy.
performerDemands: Concealment and double meaning: playing characters who hide their true allegiance, often with accents, disguises and action work.

label: Experimental
definition: A mode of filmmaking, also called avant-garde cinema, that does not apply standard cinematic conventions, adopting non-narrative forms or alternatives to traditional narratives and methods.
performerDemands: Openness to non-naturalistic, abstract or movement-based performance without conventional character or story.

label: Exploitation
definition: A film that seeks commercial success by capitalising on current trends, niche genres or sensational content such as sex, violence and the bizarre, usually on a low budget.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exploitation_film (Wikipedia; Dartmouth College film-genre research guide also listed)
performerDemands: Broad, uninhibited performance on fast, low-budget shoots, often including nudity, violence and stunt work.

label: Fairy Tale
definition: A wonder tale involving marvellous elements and occurrences, though not necessarily about fairies, embracing both popular folktales and later invented art tales.
performerDemands: Archetypal, slightly heightened characterisation with clear moral contrast, often in costume and prosthetics.

label: Family
definition: A film genre with content appropriate for younger viewers but made to appeal to a wide range of ages, often relating to children in the context of home and family.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_film (Wikipedia; The Script Lab 'Family' page also listed)
performerDemands: Warm, accessible performance pitched to children and adults at once, often working alongside child actors or animals.

label: Fantasy
definition: Imaginative fiction that relies on strangeness of setting, such as other worlds or times, and of characters, such as supernatural or unnatural beings.
performerDemands: Belief sustained in invented worlds, often acting against green screen, in prosthetics, or with invented languages and combat.

label: Farce
definition: A form of comedy that relies on highly implausible plots, stereotyped or exaggerated characters, physical humour and misunderstandings.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farce (Wikipedia; Britannica's 'farce' article seen only via search snippet, fetch was blocked)
performerDemands: Highly stylised performances and dramatic reactions with adept comic timing for wordplay, visual gags and slapstick.

label: Film Noir
definition: A film genre offering dark or fatalistic interpretations of reality, applied to US crime films of the 1940s and 1950s noted for cynical characters and stark, expressionistic lighting.
performerDemands: Cool, cynical, clipped delivery, including terse voice-over narration and archetypes such as the hard-boiled hero and the femme fatale.

label: Folk Horror
definition: A subgenre of horror that uses elements of folklore, typically rural settings, isolation, superstition, paganism and sacrifice, to invoke fear and foreboding.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_horror (Wikipedia; BFI coverage referenced in search results)
performerDemands: Slow-building unease and, for community roles, unsettling ritual performance including song, dance and folk custom.

label: Found Footage
definition: A cinematic technique and film genre in which all or most of the work is presented as recordings made by characters in the story and later found.
performerDemands: Naturalistic, often improvised acting, sometimes while the actors operate the camera themselves.

label: Gangster
definition: A motion-picture genre, originating in the United States, depicting organised crime and typically the rise and fall of criminals within criminal organisations.
performerDemands: Charismatic menace and bursts of violence, often with regional or ethnic speech patterns and urban slang.

label: Giallo
definition: An Italian crime film with murder-mystery elements, named for the yellow covers of Italian mystery paperbacks, typically featuring stylised murders, amateur sleuths and a black-gloved killer.
performerDemands: Stylised, heightened terror and suspicion, frequently with dubbed or post-synchronised dialogue.

label: Gothic Horror
definition: Horror that draws on Gothic literature, with macabre narratives set in isolated, decaying places such as castles and old houses, supernatural events and tormented characters.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_film (Wikipedia; EBSCO Research Starters 'Gothic film' also listed)
performerDemands: Heightened, period-styled emotion and dread, with period manners, speech and costume.

label: Grindhouse
definition: Grindhouse names the low-budget horror, splatter, foreign and exploitation films for adults that played in American 'grindhouse' or 'action house' theatres, and films made in imitation of them.
performerDemands: Commitment to lurid, heightened material on a low budget, often with stunt and gore-effects work done quickly and without retakes.

label: Hangout
definition: A hangout film prioritises unhurried interaction among likeable characters over forward plot momentum, so that the pleasure lies in spending time in their company.
source: https://crookedmarquee.com/on-the-singular-pleasures-of-the-hangout-movie/ (film criticism site; term popularised by Quentin Tarantino)
performerDemands: Relaxed, naturalistic ensemble chemistry and conversational ease that makes an audience want to stay with the characters.

label: Heist
definition: The heist film is a subgenre of crime film focused on the planning, execution and aftermath of a significant robbery.
performerDemands: Ensemble precision and cool, controlled tension, with each actor defining a specialist role quickly within the crew.

label: Historical Drama
definition: A historical drama is a dramatic work set in the past that presents historical events and characters with varying degrees of fiction.
performerDemands: Period manners, speech and bearing, and often the portrayal of real historical figures with credible psychology.

label: Historical Fiction
definition: Historical fiction is a genre in which a fictitious plot takes place in the setting of particular real historical events.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_fiction (Wikipedia; the article treats it as a literary genre also applied to film)
performerDemands: Period manners and speech that make invented characters feel at home in a real historical setting.

label: Holiday
definition: A holiday film is set during or built around a holiday season, most often Christmas or Thanksgiving, and trades on that season's traditions and feeling.
source: https://stuyspec.com/article/holiday-movies-what-are-they (student newspaper essay; no formal definition given, definition here is a summary)
performerDemands: Warmth and sincerity in sentimental material, often with light comic timing for family or romantic plots.

label: Hood Film
definition: Hood film is a film genre originating in the United States which features aspects of urban African American or Hispanic American culture.
performerDemands: Grounded, naturalistic performance with authentic contemporary vernacular and the emotional weight of violence and loss.

label: Horror
definition: Horror films are motion pictures calculated to cause intense repugnance, fear or dread.
performerDemands: Sustained fear and dread played convincingly, often physically demanding screaming, running and reacting to effects that are not there on set.

label: Horror Comedy
definition: Comedy horror is a film and television genre that combines elements of comedy and horror fiction.
performerDemands: Holding both registers at once: comic timing alongside genuine fear, often by playing absurd situations straight.

label: Isekai
definition: Isekai ('another world') is a subgenre of Japanese fantasy and science fiction about a person or people transported to, and having to survive in, another world.
performerDemands: Mostly voice acting: a modern, relatable everyman voice reacting to fantastical rules, often with comic asides.

label: Jidaigeki
definition: Jidaigeki is a genre of Japanese film, television and theatre set in the past, typically the Edo period, with an established set of dramatic conventions.
performerDemands: A contrived, formal, archaic register of Japanese speech, stylised makeup and catchphrases, and choreographed sword combat.

label: Jukebox Musical
definition: A jukebox musical is a stage musical or musical film whose featured songs are mostly already well-known popular songs rather than an original score.
performerDemands: Singing and dancing to familiar pop songs, making well-known numbers serve character and story rather than imitation of the original artist.

label: Kaiju
definition: Kaiju ('strange beast') eiga is a subgenre of Japanese monster film featuring giant creatures, typically attacking cities.
performerDemands: For human cast, reacting to unseen giant threats; for suit actors, physical performance inside stiff latex creature suits on miniature sets.

label: Kitchen Sink Drama
definition: Kitchen sink realism is a British cultural movement of the late 1950s and early 1960s depicting working-class lives, often through disillusioned 'angry young men'.
performerDemands: Unglamorous naturalism, regional working-class speech and contained anger in cramped domestic settings.

label: Legal Drama
definition: Legal drama is a genre of film and television focused on narratives about legal practice and the justice system.
performerDemands: Commanding delivery of long, technical speeches such as closing arguments and cross-examinations.

label: Magical Realism
definition: Magical realism is a style or genre that presents a realistic view of the world while incorporating magical elements, blurring the line between the fantastic and the real.
performerDemands: Playing the marvellous with complete matter-of-factness, keeping a grounded realist register amid the impossible.

label: Martial Arts
definition: Martial arts films are a subgenre of action film featuring martial arts combat between characters.
performerDemands: Real martial arts skill or extensive fight training, choreography and stunt work, sometimes aided by wire work and doubles.

label: Medical Drama
definition: A medical drama is a film or television programme whose events centre on a hospital, clinic, doctor's office or other medical setting.
performerDemands: Fluent delivery of medical jargon, convincing procedural business, and high-stakes emotion in life-and-death scenes.

label: Melodrama
definition: Melodrama is a sentimental dramatic form that emphasises exciting incidents and strong emotion, with stock characters in an improbable plot, over character development.
performerDemands: Heightened emotion and exaggerated performance that commits fully to high stakes without irony.

label: Military
definition: A military film centres on armed forces and military life; no separate reference definition was found, and the nearest, the war film, is a genre concerned with warfare with combat scenes central to the drama.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film (Wikipedia; used as nearest genre, no standalone 'military film' entry found)
performerDemands: Military bearing, drill and weapons handling, often learned in a pre-shoot boot camp, plus ensemble camaraderie.

label: Mockumentary
definition: A mockumentary is a film or television programme depicting fictional events presented as a documentary.
performerDemands: Deadpan naturalism and improvisation, including talking-head interviews played as if unaware of the joke.

label: Monster Movie
definition: A monster movie is a film that focuses on characters struggling to survive attacks by one or more antagonistic monsters.
performerDemands: Sustained fear and physical survival action, often reacting to a creature added later in effects.

label: Mumblecore
definition: Mumblecore is a subgenre of low-budget independent film characterised by naturalistic acting, sometimes improvised dialogue, and a focus on young adults' personal relationships.
performerDemands: Naturalism in performance and dialogue, frequently improvised, often by non-professional or lightly trained actors.

label: Musical
definition: A musical film is a motion picture that integrates musical numbers, sung and often danced, into its plot.
performerDemands: Singing and dance, with the ability to carry character and story through musical numbers.

label: Mystery
definition: A mystery is a narrative genre centred on unravelling the unknown, typically withholding the explanation of a puzzle or crime until the end.
performerDemands: Withholding and layering: playing characters with secrets so that clues register without giving the solution away.

label: Nature Documentary
definition: A nature or wildlife documentary is a documentary film or series about animals, plants or other non-human living things.
performerDemands: Mostly presenting and voice-over narration: clear, engaging delivery and on-camera presence with wildlife.

label: Neo-Noir
definition: Neo-noir is a film genre from the 1970s New Hollywood era onward that revives and subverts the visual style and tropes of classic film noir.
performerDemands: Cool, morally ambiguous understatement, cynical voice-over and controlled menace.

label: Neorealism
definition: Italian Neorealism was a postwar film movement known for realistic treatment of social themes, real locations, documentary-like objectivity and nonprofessional actors in leading roles.
performerDemands: Unadorned, documentary-like naturalism, with actors who are or appear to be ordinary people in everyday situations.

label: New Wave
definition: The New Wave (Nouvelle Vague) was the style of a group of highly individualistic French directors of the late 1950s, marked by location shooting, handheld cameras and elliptical editing.
performerDemands: Spontaneous, naturalistic playing with improvised dialogue, on location and in natural light.

label: Nordic Noir
definition: Nordic noir is a genre of crime fiction, usually told from a police point of view and set in Scandinavia or the Nordic countries.
performerDemands: Restrained, interior performance with bleak tone and slow-burning tension.

label: Occult
definition: A subgenre of horror, and at times of other genres, built around the Devil, witchcraft, demonic possession, exorcism and other hidden supernatural forces.
performerDemands: Asks for sustained dread and belief in unseen forces, often with extreme physical and vocal transformation in possession scenes.

label: Parody
definition: A work that imitates the style and conventions of another work, author or genre, usually to ridicule them, sometimes in admiration or as a comic exercise.
performerDemands: Asks for precise imitation of a recognisable style played with a straight face, so the exaggeration lands as comedy.

label: Period Drama
definition: A film or television production set in a past period, marked by attention to the costume, setting and language of that era.
performerDemands: Asks for period manners, etiquette and speech, often with dialect coaching to evoke the class and culture of the era.

label: Picaresque
definition: A narrative, originally a Spanish novel form, relating the episodic adventures of a lowborn rogue who drifts from place to place and through social milieus in order to survive.
performerDemands: Asks a lead to carry a loose, episodic story on charm and wit, shifting register across many settings and encounters.

label: Police Procedural
definition: A subgenre of detective fiction that emphasizes an accurate depiction of the investigative procedures of police officers or law-enforcement agencies.
performerDemands: Asks for credible professional fluency with procedure and jargon, and restraint in interrogation and ensemble scenes.

label: Political Drama
definition: A play, film or television programme with a political component, whether reflecting the author's political opinion or depicting a politician or a series of political events.
performerDemands: Asks for command of dense, rhetorical dialogue and speeches, and the quiet calculation of characters wielding power.

label: Political Thriller
definition: A thriller set against the backdrop of a political power struggle, with high stakes and suspense at the core of the story.
performerDemands: Asks for sustained tension and paranoia, conveyed largely through restraint and what characters conceal.

label: Post-Apocalyptic
definition: Speculative fiction set in a world or civilization after a catastrophe such as nuclear war, plague or other disaster has caused its collapse.
performerDemands: Asks for physical endurance and a worn, survival-hardened presence, often with little dialogue.

label: Prison Film
definition: A film genre concerned with prison life and often with prison escape.
performerDemands: Asks for confined, intense ensemble work and the psychological toll of long confinement and institutional cruelty.

label: Psychological Horror
definition: A subgenre of horror and psychological fiction that focuses on mental, emotional and psychological states to frighten, disturb or unsettle its audience.
performerDemands: Asks for portraying unstable or unreliable mental states and building dread through subtlety and ambiguity rather than spectacle.

label: Psychological Thriller
definition: A genre combining the thriller and psychological fiction, dealing with characters' mental states, perception and identity in a suspenseful setting.
performerDemands: Asks for sustained tension and layered, ambiguous performances, often of obsessive or unreliable characters.

label: Queer Cinema
definition: Films involving the representation of fictional and factual lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer people, storylines and community issues.
performerDemands: Asks for truthful, unstereotyped portrayal of identity and intimacy across whatever genre the film works in.

label: Revenge
definition: A film centred on vengeance, usually following a protagonist who has suffered a grievous wrong and pursues payback against those responsible.
source: https://nofilmschool.com/revenge-movie-genre (No Film School; Wikipedia redirects 'Revenge film' to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigilante_film)
performerDemands: Asks for a lead to carry grief turning into cold, driven obsession, frequently alongside fight and stunt work.

label: Road Movie
definition: A film genre in which the main characters leave home on a road trip, a journey that typically alters the perspective of their everyday lives.
performerDemands: Asks for intimate, dialogue-led work between travelling companions, carried in confined car scenes and gradual character change.

label: Rockumentary
definition: A documentary about rock music or rock musicians.
performerDemands: Mostly features real musicians playing themselves; asks for live musical performance and unguarded presence on camera.

label: Romance
definition: A film genre whose main plot focus is a romantic love story and the passion, emotion and involvement of its main characters through courtship or marriage.
performerDemands: Asks for on-screen chemistry, emotional openness and intimacy between the leads.

label: Romantic Comedy
definition: A film genre whose narrative is organized around the pursuit of love, depicted in a lighthearted manner, and almost always resolved happily.
performerDemands: Asks for comic timing, verbal sparring and charm combined with believable chemistry between the leads.

label: Romantic Drama
definition: An intersection of drama and romance films that explores the complex side of love, usually centring on an obstacle preventing love between two people.
performerDemands: Asks for heightened, sustained emotion and longing, often culminating in loss or separation.

label: Samurai
definition: Japanese films about samurai, closely tied to chanbara sword-fight films and the broader jidaigeki period drama set before the Meiji Restoration of 1868.
performerDemands: Asks for trained, readable stage swordplay (tate) and period bearing and stillness.

label: Satire
definition: An artistic form, chiefly literary and dramatic, in which human or individual vices, follies, abuses or shortcomings are held up to censure by ridicule, irony, parody or caricature.
performerDemands: Asks for playing absurd or venal characters with conviction and a straight face, letting the critique emerge through deadpan or caricature.

label: Science Fantasy
definition: A hybrid genre of speculative fiction that combines tropes and elements of both science fiction and fantasy.
performerDemands: Asks for committing sincerely to invented worlds, often against green screen, with occasional stylised or physical action.

label: Science Fiction
definition: A form of fiction that deals principally with the impact of actual or imagined science and technology upon society or individuals.
performerDemands: Asks for grounding technical exposition and imagined worlds in believable human reaction, frequently against effects-driven settings.

label: Screwball Comedy
definition: A film comedy, chiefly of the 1930s and 1940s, centring on seemingly mismatched lovers, eccentric characters and madcap antics in unlikely romances.
performerDemands: Asks for rapid-fire, overlapping dialogue delivered with precise timing, plus physical slapstick.

label: Sea Adventure
definition: Adventure stories set on or near the sea, focused on voyages, ships and the human relationship to the sea and nautical culture.
performerDemands: Asks for physical work in water and on ships, command of nautical language, and heroic presence.

label: Silent Film
definition: A film made without synchronized recorded sound, as in cinema from the mid-1890s to the early 1930s, typically accompanied by live music and using title cards.
performerDemands: Asks for wordless expression through pantomime, gesture and facial expression.

label: Slapstick
definition: Comedy built on broad physical action, such as falls and blows, absurd situations and vigorous, often violent action, with roots in commedia dell'arte.
performerDemands: Asks for physical comedy: precise timing, acrobatic falls and stunts, and animated facial expression.

label: Slasher
definition: A subgenre of horror in which a killer or killers stalk and murder a group of people, often with bladed tools.
performerDemands: Asks for sustained terror, screaming and chase physicality, with a 'final girl' carrying the climactic confrontation.

label: Slice Of Life
definition: A genre depicting ordinary people and the real drama of everyday life, often without a conventional plot or dramatic climax.
performerDemands: Asks for naturalistic, understated behaviour that holds attention without plot-driven big moments.

label: Social Realism
definition: Work that depicts the everyday lives and real socio-political conditions of poor and working-class people, often to critique the power structures behind them.
performerDemands: Asks for unpolished, naturalistic performance, often with improvisation and alongside non-professional actors.

label: Space Opera
definition: A subgenre of science fiction of futuristic, melodramatic adventure set among space travellers and extraterrestrial beings, usually on a galactic scale.
performerDemands: Asks for heightened, melodramatic conviction in grand stakes, often with action and effects-heavy work.

label: Spaghetti Western
definition: A subgenre of Westerns set in the 19th-century American West but made by Italian filmmakers and shot in Europe, chiefly in the 1960s and early 1970s, known for a cynical, violent outlook and antiheroic characters.
performerDemands: Asks for laconic, largely wordless presence held in extreme close-up, with menace and stillness carried by the face and eyes rather than dialogue.

label: Splatter
definition: A subgenre of horror film that deliberately focuses on graphic portrayals of gore and violence, usually through special effects.
performerDemands: Asks for committed, uninhibited physical reactions to pain and terror while working around prosthetics and stage blood.

label: Sports
definition: A film genre in which a sport, sporting event, athlete or follower of sport plays a prominent role and drives the plot or its resolution.
performerDemands: Asks for credible athletic skill and physical conditioning in the sport depicted, alongside an emotional underdog arc.

label: Spy
definition: A genre of film dealing with fictional espionage, either realistically or as a basis for fantasy, showing government agents at risk of discovery by their enemies.
performerDemands: Asks for controlled, concealed performance — playing a cover identity while signalling hidden intent — and, in action-led entries, stunt and fight work.

label: Steampunk
definition: Science fiction dealing with 19th-century societies dominated by historical or imagined steam-powered technology, often set in an alternate Victorian era.
performerDemands: Asks for Victorian period manners and speech worn alongside heavy costume and props, played with adventurous flair.

label: Stoner Comedy
definition: A subgenre of comedy film based on marijuana themes, in which recreational use often drives the plot.
performerDemands: Asks for relaxed, loose comic timing and believable altered-state behaviour, often in a double act.

label: Superhero
definition: A film genre centred on superhero characters, individuals with extraordinary abilities dedicated to fighting crime, saving the world or helping the innocent, often based on comics.
performerDemands: Asks for intensive physical training, stunt and fight work, and sustained performance against green screen and visual effects, balanced with an origin-story emotional arc.

label: Supernatural
definition: A film genre built on supernatural themes such as gods, ghosts, spirits, miracles and other phenomena that cannot be explained by rational or scientific means.
performerDemands: Asks for convincing reactions to unseen or effects-driven presences and sustained unease.

label: Surrealist
definition: A modernist approach to filmmaking that arose in Paris in the 1920s, combining shocking, irrational or absurd imagery with dreamlike symbolism to challenge the idea that art should represent reality.
performerDemands: Asks for full commitment to irrational, dream-logic situations played without explanation or psychological realism.

label: Survival
definition: A film genre, often treated as a subgenre of adventure, in which one or more characters struggle for physical survival in perilous circumstances.
performerDemands: Asks for physical endurance in harsh conditions and sustained solo performance with little dialogue.

label: Swashbuckler
definition: A film genre characterised by swordfighting and daring, adventurous heroic characters, sometimes with romantic elements.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swashbuckler_film (Wikipedia); also https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/swashbucklers (Merriam-Webster: 'a novel or drama dealing with a swashbuckler')
performerDemands: Asks for theatrical stage-combat swordplay, usually staged by a fight director, delivered with athletic bravado and period dash.
demandsSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddy_Crean (fight directors such as Paddy Crean and Ralph Faulkner staged the swordplay for Errol Flynn's swashbucklers; search snippet)

label: Sword And Sandal
definition: Also called peplum, a subgenre of largely Italian-made historical, mythological or biblical epics set mostly in Greco-Roman antiquity, dominant in Italy from about 1958 to 1965.
performerDemands: Asks for a muscular physique and feats of strength, declamatory ancient-world delivery, and sword combat.

label: Sword And Sorcery
definition: A subgenre of fantasy featuring sword-wielding heroes in violent adventures involving magic and the supernatural, focused on personal battles rather than world-endangering stakes.
performerDemands: Asks for physical weapon combat, a heroic physicality, and heightened mythic delivery.

label: Techno-Thriller
definition: A thriller whose plot relies on modern technology, drawing on science fiction, spy and military fiction and supported by detailed technical material.
performerDemands: Asks for fluent, credible delivery of dense technical jargon under sustained tension.

label: Teen
definition: A film genre aimed at teenagers and young adults whose plots concern their lives, such as coming of age, first love, rebellion, conflict with parents and alienation.
performerDemands: Asks for believable adolescent behaviour and emotional volatility, often from actors older than the characters.

label: Thriller
definition: A broad genre that evokes excitement and suspense, building tension around menacing situations in which escape seems impossible.
performerDemands: Asks for sustained tension, restraint and fear played under pressure.

label: Time Travel
definition: A subgenre of science fiction or fantasy in which characters journey to the past or future, using time travel to explore paradoxes and altered histories.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel_in_fiction (Wikipedia; definition sentence came from a nofilmschool.com result in the same search)
performerDemands: Asks for playing a fish out of water across eras, sometimes several versions of one character.

label: Tokusatsu
definition: A Japanese term for live-action films or television programmes that make heavy use of practical special effects, such as kaiju films and transforming-hero series.
performerDemands: Asks for suit acting: stunt and fight work performed inside a full costume that hides the face, with character conveyed through body movement and the voice dubbed later.

label: Tragedy
definition: A branch of drama that treats in a serious and dignified style the sorrowful or terrible events encountered or caused by a heroic individual.
performerDemands: Asks for heightened emotion at scale and dignity in suffering, carrying a character to a catastrophic end.

label: Tragicomedy
definition: A dramatic work incorporating both tragic and comic elements.
source: https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/tragicomedy (Britannica Dictionary; Britannica's art article quoted in the same result)
performerDemands: Asks for shifting tone between comic and serious, often within one scene, while keeping the tragic stakes real.
demandsSource: https://www.studiobinder.com/blog/what-is-tragicomedy-definition/ (search snippet; general genre guide, not acting-specific)

label: True Crime
definition: A non-fiction genre across literature, film and television that examines actual crimes, especially murder, and their investigation and prosecution.
performerDemands: In dramatised form, asks for portraying real people with accuracy and restraint.

label: Vampire
definition: Films about vampires, folkloric beings who feed on the life essence or blood of the living, most often within horror but also in drama, romance, comedy and other genres.
performerDemands: Asks for a seductive, otherworldly stillness and menace, often with period manners and prosthetic fangs.

label: War
definition: A film genre concerned with warfare, typically land, sea or air battles, with combat scenes central to the drama.
performerDemands: Asks for military bearing and drill, physical endurance in combat sequences, and depiction of trauma and camaraderie.

label: Werewolf
definition: Fiction and film portraying werewolves, humans who shapeshift into wolves or wolflike creatures, often by curse or bite and triggered by the full moon.
performerDemands: Asks for physical transformation performance and endurance of long hours in heavy prosthetic makeup.
demandsSource: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/wolf-man-star-christopher-abbott-1236109770/ (Hollywood Reporter on a seven-hour transformation makeup; search snippet)

label: Western
definition: A genre of novels, stories, films and television set in the American West, usually between the 1850s and the end of the 19th century.
performerDemands: Asks for horsemanship, gun handling and a laconic frontier manner.

label: Whodunit
definition: A detective or mystery story, presented as a novel, play or film, built around discovering who committed a crime.
performerDemands: Asks for ensemble playing in which each suspect plausibly conceals something, and for the detective, clear delivery of deductive exposition.

label: Wuxia
definition: A genre of Chinese fiction and low fantasy concerning the adventures of martial artists in ancient China, bound by a code of chivalry.
performerDemands: Asks for martial-arts training and wire-assisted acrobatics to stage choreographed, physics-defying swordplay.
demandsSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuxia (King Hu and Shaw Brothers films used wire- and trampoline-assisted acrobatics; read directly) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wire_fu (search snippet)

label: Yakuza
definition: A Japanese film genre focused on the lives and dealings of the yakuza, Japan's organized crime syndicates.
performerDemands: Asks for codified gangster bearing and ritual manners, torn between duty and feeling in chivalry films or raw violence in the 1970s realist cycle.

label: Zombie
definition: A film genre featuring creatures usually portrayed as reanimated corpses or virally infected humans, commonly cannibalistic, mostly within horror.
performerDemands: For the undead, asks for trained, consistent creature movement under makeup; for the living, sustained fear and survival physicality.
